learningObjective: Predict the behavior of `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` when the traced code triggers a graph break.

canonicalClaims.claim: `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` requires whole-function capture; any construct that would cause a graph break raises an exception rather than splitting the graph.
nonImplications: Does not imply every fullgraph=True model fails; well-authored models compile.
Does not imply fullgraph=True is a performance flag; it is a correctness/verification flag.

misconceptions.claim: fullgraph=True falls back to eager when a break would occur.
misconceptions.whyWrong: No fallback; the exception is raised.

misconceptions.claim: fullgraph=True yields the same split-subgraph structure as fullgraph=False.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Split subgraphs are exactly what fullgraph=True disallows.

misconceptions.claim: fullgraph=True is a runtime performance optimization only.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is primarily a correctness/verification flag; performance benefit is indirect (no eager gaps).

implementationFacts: Common break triggers: print, list mutations of externals, data-dependent branches, unsupported ops
The error names the offending bytecode / op for developer cleanup
fullgraph=True is often used as a CI check on production models
performanceScenarios: Eliminating graph breaks lets the compiled function run without eager gaps; fullgraph=True enforces this at CI level.
